Hesap birimi: The function and property of money being used as a unit of account in transactions of exchange and accounting.
Hesap birimi maliyeti: Inflation making money less reliable as a unit-of-account measure.
Hesap Verebilirlik: Means that central banks are accountable to society for the decisions they take, their consequences and their corporate governance. Accountability is a requirement of central bank independence and can be fulfilled in various ways. These are listed as the obligations set by law, internal and external audits, and the transparency and communication policies implemented by central banks.
Heterojen oligopol: An oligopoly market in which a differentiated product is bought and sold.
High Level Objective, Intermediate: Outcomes, Immediate Outcomes. High Level Effectiveness: the high effectiveness degree showing, in the assessment made of the country's anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing system, that the short-term outcomes were largely achieved but that minor corrections are needed. High Level Mission: the 'high level visit' stage in the enhanced follow-up process applied by the FATF Plenary following the FATF country assessment, on account of the presence of certain factors relating to the country.
Hisse başına kâr: The profit per share found by dividing net profit by the number of paid-in capital shares; it is calculated by deducting preferential dividends.
Hizmet: Products that cannot be touched or stored, or that do not create ownership.
HİSER Destek Programı: The Service Sector Competitiveness Enhancement Project Support, the support type provided by the Ministry of Trade within the scope of supporting foreign-currency-earning services trade. IPA: the Instrument for Pre-Accession Financial Assistance, the financial and technical assistance instrument designed by the European Commission to support reforms in EU candidate countries. IPARD: the rural development component of the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance established by the European Union (EU) to support candidate and potential candidate countries.
Hollanda hastalığı: The problem of the decline, or failure to develop, of other sectors such as industry in a country as a result of rapid enrichment based on natural resources.
Hollanda tipi ihale: Or the descending price auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively lowered, starting from a high price, until a buyer emerges.
Homogenous Products: Homogeneous products are spoken of in cases where the products substitute one another exactly and consumers perceive no de facto or real differences among the products offered by different undertakings. Price is the most important element for which undertakings producing homogeneous products compete. Empirical findings show that, when the number of undertakings is small, the existence of homogeneous products can facilitate tacit agreement. Horizontal Differentiation: Undertakings diversifying their products according to elements such as color, design and location, trying to reach consumer groups with different styles and tastes. For example, within the same media group, different newspapers appealing to different preferences in society, such as a tabloid, an opinion newspaper and a mass-market newspaper, can be published.
Hostile Takeover: In such acquisitions, which are one way for an undertaking to gain control of another undertaking's shares, the acquiring undertaking, without the knowledge or consent of the target undertaking's managers, becomes partly or wholly owner of the said undertaking by agreeing with a portion of its shareholders or by accumulating shares from the stock exchange.
Hızlandırıcı Programı: The support program applied to accelerate the development of technological products and technology-intensive start-up (early-stage) ventures. Support is given on matters such as hardware and operational expenses for activities like expansion into international markets, increasing exports, and taking part in advanced entrepreneurship ecosystems. Grant Support: the support type given without repayment.
IBOR ya da bankalararası faiz oranı: The interest rate banks pay one another in the money market for their daily uncollateralized borrowings.
Increasing Returns to Scale: Returns to scale can be defined as the effect on efficiency of the change occurring in the scale of production. Increasing returns to scale is the situation in which the undertaking's average cost falls as the quantity produced rises. There are two sources of this fall. The first is internal, stemming from the increase in the undertaking's level of production. The second is external; accordingly, the increase in the quantity of production in the industry affects the prices in the market in a way that will cause the undertaking to change its production decision
Indirect Control on Prices: Indirect price control comprises practices such as profit control at the product and/or producer level and cost-efficiency pricing, in which the price is not set directly by the regulatory authority, but the producer's freedom to set prices is restricted.
Industrial Design: Design is the bringing together, regularly and purposefully, of more or fewer parts.
Innovation: Innovation encompasses all the activities in creating a new product or production process, from scientific research through invention, development and commercialization. Scientific research is the new knowledge developing in the mind without a particular use being considered; invention is the application of scientific knowledge to reach a particular aim, including prototype model making; and development is the correction of the prototype so that it can be offered for consumer use, toward the final product or process.
Innovative Markets: The markets where undertakings whose futures depend on their success in creating intangible goods, and which are quite sensitive to other undertakings' successful innovations, are found are innovative markets. Innovativeness is closely related to today's information age or revolution. Being able to create new (technological) knowledge depends on defining and integrating the different, mutually complementary pieces of information that are the inputs of this process. The recombination of the pieces of information belonging to the past and to the whole, the new knowledge
Intellectual Property Rights: The absolute-quality rights over the elements constituting the subject of intellectual property, such as literary and artistic works, patents, utility models, designs, trademarks and integrated circuit topographies. The holder of an intellectual property right obtains exclusive authorities against its rivals and, as a result, can prevent the unauthorized use of the intellectual property subject it holds. An undertaking's being a monopoly in the production and sale of a product by virtue of the intellectual property right it holds is the dominant position issue in competition law
Investigation: The rights of the undertakings under investigation, such as the right to be informed, the right to protection of trade secrets, the right to a reasoned decision, the right to litigate and the right of defense.
IS eğrisi: A graphical tool showing the relationship between total production and the interest rate when the goods market in the economy is in equilibrium.
IS-LM dengesi: The situation in which, in a given period, the goods markets and the money markets in the economy are in equilibrium at the same time.
ISIC Kodu: The international standard industrial classification used by the United Nations to classify economic data.
işsiz: Persons aged 15 and over who are not in employment, who have used at least one of the active job-search channels within the last four weeks, and who could start work within two weeks.
İdaresi Başkanlığı): A public organization with legal personality and a special budget, related to the Ministry of Industry and Technology, established with the aim of increasing the share and effectiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises in meeting the country's economic and social needs, raising their competitive strengths and levels, and realizing integration in industry in a manner consistent with economic developments. Credit: the provision or transfer of purchasing power to someone, on the condition of taking it back after a certain period.
İhale: In market economies, one of the methods of allocating various goods and financial values to individuals or institutions. In particular, if the good to be auctioned has no fixed or directly determinable price, or if the seller of the good is unsure about the good's market price, sale by auction eliminates this uncertainty under fully competitive conditions. Auctions can be conducted in different forms. The most common are the multiple-price (Dutch Auction) type auctions in which prices are ordered from largest to smallest, ensuring maximum revenue and minimum cost for the seller. In this auction, the transaction with each participant is made at the price it itself bid. Auctions in which prices are ordered from smallest to largest are called the 'English Auction'. Another auction method is the 'single price' auction. In this auction type, the price at which supply and demand are equated is applied to all the participants winning the auction. In other words, all the transactions are carried out at a single price. Both auction types have advantages and disadvantages relative to one another. In the single price auction, the cost of information gathering is lower and greater participation can be achieved. In the multiple price auction, more intense competition is in question and a lower cost may be in question for the seller. However, all these depend on the structure of the market and the conditions of the day.
İhale kuramı: The body of principles explaining how economic units behave under different conditions in purchases and sales made with the best bidding method.
İhracat: The selling of goods to other countries by the persons and institutions resident in a country.
İhracat Destek Ofisi: The offices established with the aim of guiding exporters or those wanting to start exporting, which have begun to be implemented in selected provinces with a project launched in cooperation between TOBB and the Ministry of Trade.
İhracat fonksiyonu: The mathematical relationship showing how the quantity of exports changes, depending on various variables, in an economy.
İhracat Reeskont Kredisi: Within the framework of the rediscount regulations issued pursuant to Article 45 of the CBRT Law, export rediscount credit is extended by the CBRT in return for the rediscounting by intermediary banks of bills drawn in foreign currency by firms and meeting certain conditions. Export rediscount credits are extended through the TL counterpart of the foreign currency amount stated in the bill, at the rate announced on the date the credit is extended, being paid to the firms via banks. Since the repayment of the credits at maturity occurs in foreign currency, a significant contribution is made to the CBRT's foreign currency reserves.
İhracatın İthalatı Karşılama Oranı: The Coverage Ratio is calculated with the formula (Exports / Imports) * 100. The coverage ratio being greater than 100 shows that the country has a foreign trade surplus; being less than 100 shows that it has a foreign trade deficit.
İhraç edilen menkul kıymet: According to the CBRT definition, the bonds and bills issued by banks with maturities of up to two years.
İkame esnekliği: A basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the ratio of the quantities of two variables to each other changes as a result of a one percent increase in the ratio of the prices of these two variables.
İkame etkisi: The change seen when the price of a product or input changes, due to its becoming relatively cheaper or more expensive beside its substitute.
İkame mal: Products that can be used in place of one another to a certain extent.
İkinci derece fiyat ayrımcılığı: The practice of selling different quantities of a certain product at different prices.
İkinci fiyat kapalı teklif ihalesi: A type of auction in which participants submit sealed bids and the highest bidder wins and pays the second-highest price.
İkincil Gelir Hesabı: The secondary income account contains the transfers defined as the provision, unrequited, by a unit resident domestically (abroad) to a unit resident abroad (domestically) of a real resource such as a good or service, or of a financial asset.
İkincil Piyasa: Refers to the markets where instruments trade after their initial issuance. Borsa Istanbul's Debt Securities Market, where the debt securities issued by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye are bought and sold after issuance, is an example of a secondary market.
İktisadi Yönelim Anketi - İYA: A survey applied monthly with the aim of producing indicators that will reflect the short-term tendencies of manufacturing industry, by monitoring the assessments of the recent past, the views on the current situation and the forward-looking expectations of the senior managers of workplaces operating in manufacturing industry, on matters such as production, exports and domestic market orders, investment and employment. To access the Business Tendency Survey and the Real Sector Confidence Index
İktisat: Or by its other name economics: the branch of science researching how individuals and societies use the limited resources at their disposal to meet their broad wants and needs.
İleride teslim kuru: The rate or interest agreed today and fixed for a transaction to be realized at a future date; also used in non-deliverable derivatives.
İmalat Sanayi Kapasite Kullanım Oranı: An indicator produced on the basis of the results of the Business Tendency Survey, aiming to capture the actual capacity utilization of workplaces operating in the manufacturing industry sector in the relevant period according to their existing physical capacities. To access the Manufacturing Industry Capacity Utilization Rate
İmar Planı: The maps prepared by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization and the local governments for the planned structuring of settlements, on which areas such as industry-commerce-housing-public services-green space-agricultural land-protection areas are marked.
İmmünizasyon: The strategy of protection against interest risk by equalizing the durations of assets and liabilities; it is the fundamental instrument of bank asset-liability management.
İmza Sirküleri: The document determining the areas of authority and responsibility of the persons acting on behalf of the relevant organization, prepared upon application by legal persons to the notary. For natural persons, instead of this document, a signature declaration document is drawn up. Innovation: the realization of a new or significantly improved good, service, process or method. Usufruct: the right of use granted to certain person or persons over a good or right whose ownership belongs to someone else.
İngiliz tipi ihale: Or the ascending price auction: a type of auction in which participants make open bids and the price is progressively raised, starting from a low price, until the winner is determined.
